findings.evidence: 14-pos-parked-orders.network.json contains 7 entries with status 429 (GET /api/admin/pos/walk-in-customer ×2, GET /api/admin/users/address/28, POST /api/admin/users, GET /api/admin/users?...Client%20Comptoir, GET /api/admin/pos/parked-orders ×2). 14-pos-parked-orders.console.json has 7 matching 'Failed to load resource: 429' errors. 14-pos-parked-orders.dom.html (after stripping <style> and <script> blocks) contains ZERO elements matching swal2-popup, .toast, .alert-*, .v-toast, .Toastify, [role=alert], .iziToast, .noty, or .snackbar. The cashier never sees that customer/parked-orders endpoints failed. State 15-pos-logout repeats the pattern (2× 429 on /api/admin/pos/counter-collect/pending and /api/admin/oss-order). Per REVIEWER_PROTOCOL.md category 6 (silent_error → P0) and category 10 (unexpected_4xx not in allowlist → P0).
findings.fix_hint: Two surfaces involved. (1) Backend rate-limit configuration: app/Http/Kernel.php throttle:api appears to be too aggressive for the POS resume-from-tracker re-mount sequence (it fires walk-in-customer + parked-orders + users in <500ms). Bump throttle on /api/admin/pos/* and /api/admin/users for authenticated POS operator role, or implement client-side debounce. (2) Frontend silent-failure: resources/js/components/admin/pos/ParkedOrdersComponent.vue (mounted/loadParked) and PosComponent.vue's walk-in customer fetch must surface a SweetAlert2 toast or Vuex notify('error') on 429 — currently the axios interceptor swallows 429 specifically without firing toast. Check resources/js/axios-interceptors or the global axios instance in resources/js/app.js for status===429 short-circuit.

findings.evidence: State 15 PNG visibly renders English text on a French app: 'Welcome Back' (h2), 'Email' label, 'Password' label, 'Remember Me' (checkbox label), 'Forget Password' link, 'Login' button label, 'Log In' top-right CTA. State 01 PNG of the same /login page shows 'Bon Retour', 'Mot De Passe', 'Se Souvenir De Moi', 'Mot De Passe Oublié', 'Connexion'. 15-pos-logout.dom.html captured AFTER the screenshot does contain French ('Bon retour', 'Mot de passe', 'Connexion') — meaning the page hydrated French AFTER the visible English flash. This is a Flash-Of-Unstyled-Content for locale: the cashier sees English for ~300-700ms during the logout→/login redirect. State 15 PNG also captures spinner bars beneath the Login button — confirming mid-transition. The HTML lang attribute is 'fr' so the SSR shell is correct; the i18n bundle resolves AFTER the initial paint.
findings.fix_hint: Two-pronged fix. (1) Server-render the login form copy in the active locale (Blade render rather than client-side i18n() resolution) so first paint is correct French. resources/views/auth/login.blade.php should use {{ __('login.welcome_back') }} for h2, label, button. (2) If a Vue component owns the form, hoist the i18n strings into a <noscript>/SSR fallback OR delay paint until i18n.global.locale is set. Check resources/js/components/Frontend/auth/LoginComponent.vue and the Vue i18n bootstrap in resources/js/app.js — the locale guard runs after the first render tick. Repro: hit /login in a fresh tab with Network throttling 'Slow 3G' and observe English flash.

findings.evidence: tests/e2e/test-e2e-pos-kds-sync-2026-05-10-wave-A.spec.js contains 10 instances of `.catch(() => {})` (silent swallow): lines 164, 170, 173, 230, 252, 280, 285, 286, 443, 538, 614, 640, 641, 680, 681 (grep count: 10 unique callsites). Several wrap critical interactions: line 252 wraps `addToCartBtn.isVisible()` decision — if it throws, no error logged, fallback path runs blind. Line 443 wraps `trackerBtn.isVisible()` — if tracker button query throws (DOM hot-swap), state 10 silently skips the click. Lines 680/681 wrap clearCookies + storage clear during logout fallback — if those fail, state 15 may capture authenticated stale page rather than logged-out form. Per REVIEWER_PROTOCOL category 'audit_integrity', silent catches that swallow assertion-relevant errors degrade evidence quality.
findings.fix_hint: Replace `.catch(() => {})` with `.catch((e) => observations.push(`<state-id>: <action> threw ${e.message}`))` for every callsite. This preserves the resilient flow but surfaces the failure in the observations dump (which the reviewer reads). For the truly best-effort hover/focus calls (lines 170, 173) leave them silent BUT add a comment `// best-effort hover, headless may not honor :hover`. Critical paths (252, 443, 538, 680, 681) MUST log.
